reference: Installed util-linux wall for option-error statuses. Bash metadata and implementation-specific help content are explicit contracts; util-linux help wording is not copied or counted as parity. All runnable options return before any utmp or terminal access.
coverage: Bash identifies wall as a builtin and exposes its registered short help description.
Util-linux wall option-error statuses, plus explicit help contracts with no terminal broadcast.
Deferred operational coverage for controlled utmp records and terminal destinations.
exclusions: No broadcast or terminal-write operation was executed; these require a disposable PTY or syscall mock with all targets controlled.
Group filtering, duplicate utmp records, message escaping, banners, and the messages-disabled gate remain unqualified.
Help wording differs from util-linux and is checked as an implementation-specific contract.
Timeout values are validated but synchronous terminal writes do not yet enforce a deadline; no timeout/broadcast behavior is claimed.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify the registered wall command as a builtin, even with an empty executable search path.
Bash help must expose the registered short help string for wall.
Both help spellings succeed, document the supported interface and its timeout limitation, and return before any system accounting or terminal access.
cases.script:
a=$(wall --help)
b=$(wall -h)
[[ $a == "$b" ]]
[[ $a == *"Broadcast a message to every logged-in terminal"* ]]
[[ $a == *"wall -h|--help"* ]]
[[ $a == *"synchronous writes have no deadline"* ]]
printf "help ok\n"

cases.purpose: An unknown option must be rejected before any message delivery or system-path access.
A nonnumeric timeout must be rejected by option parsing before any message delivery or utmp access.
Qualify wall's operational broadcast behavior only in a disposable environment where every utmp entry and destination is controlled.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed PTY/syscall mock. Provide only synthetic USER_PROCESS utmp records and private terminal endpoints, then verify recipient selection, per-terminal de-duplication, message escaping and CRLF handling, banner suppression, and the messages-disabled gate. No broadcast was executed in this suite.
